units.grammar: Present simple and continuous. Use the present simple for habits, routines and facts: 'My cousin plays basketball on Saturdays.' 'Cats hate water.' With he, she and it add -s or -es (goes, watches, studies). Use don't / doesn't for negatives and do / does for questions: 'Does Leo like pizza?' Make the present continuous with am / is / are + verb-ing. Use it for things happening now or around now: 'Shh, the baby is sleeping.'
existing_questions_sample: My dad ____ (cook) dinner every Sunday. | cooks
Look! The children ____ (build) a snowman. | are building
____ your sister play the piano? (Do / Does) | Does
We ____ (not / have) lessons on Saturdays. | don't have
Correct it: Mia go to the gym. | Mia goes to the gym.
Be quiet, please. Grandpa ____ (sleep). | is sleeping
Water ____ (freeze) at zero degrees. | freezes
I ____ chocolate. (love / am loving) | love
Marta ____ (study) in the library this week. | is studying
How often ____ Tom visit you? (do / does) | does
Correct it: I am not knowing the answer. | I don't know the answer.
My cousins ____ (come) to stay next Friday. It's all arranged. | are coming

units.grammar: Past simple. Regular verbs add -ed (walked). Verbs ending in -e add only -d (danced); consonant + y changes to -ied (carried); a short vowel + consonant doubles the consonant (stopped). Many common verbs are irregular and you have to learn them: go - went, buy - bought, see - saw, take - took. The form is the same for every person: 'I arrived late and they arrived late too.'
existing_questions_sample: We ____ (watch) a great film last night. | watched
Lucy ____ (go) to Paris two years ago. | went
I ____ (not / see) you at the party. | didn't see
____ you finish your project yesterday? (Did / Were) | Did
Correct it: He buyed a new phone. | He bought a new phone.
They ____ (be) very tired after the match. | were
My grandmother ____ (carry) all the bags. | carried
Correct it: Did she went home? | Did she go home?
It ____ (not / be) cold last weekend. | wasn't
Dan ____ (take) lots of photos on holiday. | took
Where ____ you born? (was / were / did) | were
We ____ (stop) at a café for lunch. | stopped

units.grammar: Comparatives and superlatives. Short adjectives: add -er / the -est (cheap, cheaper, the cheapest). After -e add only -r / -st (large, larger). After one vowel + one consonant, double the consonant (hot, hotter, the hottest). Two-syllable adjectives ending in -y change y to i: easy, easier, the easiest. Longer adjectives use more / the most: 'Maths is more difficult than art.' 'It's the most exciting game I know.'
existing_questions_sample: A plane is ____ (fast) than a train. | faster
This is the ____ (funny) video on the internet. | funniest
Today's exam was ____ (bad) than the last one. | worse
Gold is ____ (expensive) than silver. | more expensive
Correct it: She is more tall than me. | She is taller than me.
August is the ____ (hot) month here. | hottest
My room isn't as big ____ yours. (as / than / that) | as
Who is the ____ (good) player in your team? | best
It's the longest river ____ the world. (in / of / than) | in
Correct it: This is the most easy question. | This is the easiest question.
The bus is slower than the train. = The bus is not ____ the train. (use fast) | as fast as
Your bag is ____ (heavy) than mine. | heavier

units.grammar: Past continuous. Form: was / were + verb-ing. 'I was reading.' 'They were laughing.' Negative: wasn't / weren't + -ing. Questions: Was / Were + subject + -ing? 'Were you listening?' Short answers: 'Yes, I was.' / 'No, we weren't.' Use it for an action in progress at a moment in the past: 'At nine o'clock last night we were having dinner.'
existing_questions_sample: At 8 pm I ____ (do) my homework. | was doing
The dogs ____ (bark) all night. | were barking
She ____ (not / listen) to the teacher. | wasn't listening
____ they playing football at lunchtime? (Was / Were / Did) | Were
Correct it: We was waiting outside. | We were waiting outside.
What ____ you doing at midnight? (was / were / did) | were
My brother ____ (swim) in the lake at noon. | was swimming
'Was it raining?' 'No, it ____.' | wasn't
The students ____ (not / wear) uniforms that day. | weren't wearing
Correct it: He was runing fast. | He was running fast.
In this old photo, Grandma ____ (smile) at the camera. | was smiling
'Were you sleeping?' 'Yes, I ____.' | was

units.grammar: Past simple and continuous. Past continuous = a longer action in progress in the past. Past simple = a short, finished action. Used together, the long action (continuous) is interrupted by the short one (simple): 'I was having a shower when the phone rang.' when usually introduces the past simple action; while usually introduces the past continuous action: 'While we were walking home, it started to rain.'
existing_questions_sample: I ____ (walk) home when I saw the accident. | was walking
She was cooking when the lights ____ (go) out. | went
While Dad ____ (drive), I fell asleep. | was driving
We were playing cards ____ the teacher came in. (when / while) | when
Sam ____ (break) his arm while he was skating. | broke
What were you doing when I ____ (call) you? | called
Correct it: I was knowing the answer. | I knew the answer.
____ I was tidying my room, I found ten euros. (While / During) | While
They ____ (not / look) when Marta scored the goal. | weren't looking
When the film ended, we ____ (go) home. | went
It ____ (rain) when we left the house, so we took umbrellas. | was raining
The phone rang while I ____ (have) breakfast. | was having

units.unit_title: some/any, much/many, a lot of, a few / a little
units.grammar: some/any, much/many, a lot of, a few / a little. some: positive sentences, with plural and uncountable nouns ('some apples', 'some rice'). any: negatives and most questions ('We haven't got any eggs.' 'Is there any juice?'). a lot of = a large amount. It works with countable and uncountable nouns in all kinds of sentence: 'She has a lot of friends and a lot of energy.'
existing_questions_sample: There isn't ____ milk in the fridge. (some / any) | any
I bought ____ new pens yesterday. (some / any) | some
How ____ students are there in your class? (much / many) | many
We haven't got ____ time. Hurry up! (much / many) | much
Can I have ____ sugar in my tea? (a few / a little) | a little
Only ____ people came to the meeting. (a few / a little) | a few
Correct it: How many money have you got? | How much money have you got?
Are there ____ good shops near here? (some / any) | any
She drinks ____ water every day. (a lot of / many) | a lot of
He gave me ____ good advice. (a few / a little) | a little
There aren't ____ buses at night. (much / many) | many
Correct it: We don't have some bread. | We don't have any bread.

units.grammar: have to and must; should. have to + infinitive = it is necessary, often because of a rule. It changes form: has to, had to. 'Nurses often have to work at night.' must + infinitive (no to, no -s) also means it is necessary, often in the speaker's opinion. It has no past form: use had to. 'I must phone Gran.' mustn't = it is not allowed: 'You mustn't run in the corridor.'
existing_questions_sample: You ____ use your phone in the exam. It's forbidden. (mustn't / don't have to) | mustn't
Tomorrow is a holiday, so we ____ go to school. (mustn't / don't have to) | don't have to
My sister ____ (have to) wear a uniform at her school. | has to
Yesterday I ____ (have to) stay late after class. | had to
You look tired. You ____ go to bed early. (should / shouldn't) | should
Correct it: He must to study more. | He must study more.
Correct it: She should goes home. | She should go home.
____ you have to help at home? (Do / Must / Are) | Do
You ____ eat so many sweets. They're bad for your teeth. (should / shouldn't) | shouldn't
Correct it: Does he has to work? | Does he have to work?
Entry is free. You ____ pay. (mustn't / don't have to) | don't have to
Correct it: We musted leave early. | We had to leave early.

units.unit_title: Future: be going to and present continuous
units.grammar: Future: be going to and present continuous. Use the present continuous for definite arrangements, usually with a time, a place or other people: 'We're meeting Carla at six.' Use be going to + infinitive for intentions, things you have decided to do: 'I'm going to learn the guitar this year.' be going to is also for predictions when you can see the evidence now: 'Watch out! That glass is going to fall.'
existing_questions_sample: I ____ going to buy a new bike. (am / is / are) | am
Look at that sky! It ____ (rain). Use going to. | is going to rain
We ____ (fly) to Rome on Friday. We've got the tickets. Use the present continuous. | are flying
____ she going to invite Pablo? (Is / Are / Does) | Is
Correct it: I going to call him. | I am going to call him.
They ____ going to come to the party. (isn't / aren't) | aren't
What time ____ you meeting the dentist tomorrow? (do / are / will) | are
Correct it: She is going to studies medicine. | She is going to study medicine.
Careful! You ____ (drop) those plates! Use going to. | are going to drop
'Are you going to watch the match?' 'Yes, I ____.' | am
My parents ____ (have) dinner with friends tonight. Use the present continuous. | are having
He hasn't studied at all. He ____ (fail) the test. Use going to. | is going to fail

units.grammar: Present perfect. Form: have / has + past participle. 'I've finished.' 'She hasn't arrived.' 'Have they eaten?' Regular past participles end in -ed, the same as the past simple. Irregular ones must be learned: see - saw - seen, write - wrote - written, do - did - done. Use it for past actions that are connected to now, when the exact time is not said: 'I've lost my keys' (= I can't find them now).
existing_questions_sample: I ____ (finish) my homework. Can I go out now? | have finished
My brother ____ (never / fly) in a plane. | has never flown
____ you ever eaten snails? (Have / Did / Has) | Have
She ____ (not / see) this film. | hasn't seen
Correct it: He have broken his leg. | He has broken his leg.
Write the past participle of 'write'. | written
'Have you ever been to Italy?' 'No, I ____.' | haven't
Mum isn't here. She has ____ to the shops. (been / gone) | gone
I've ____ to Paris twice. It's beautiful. (been / gone) | been
Correct it: I have never saw snow. | I have never seen snow.
We ____ (lose) the map. Now we can't find the way. | have lost
Write the past participle of 'take'. | taken

units.unit_title: Present perfect and past simple; How long? and for/since
units.grammar: Present perfect and past simple; How long? and for/since. Present perfect: experiences in your life up to now, with no finished time mentioned. 'I've visited Rome.' Past simple: when you say exactly when, with finished time words such as yesterday, last year, in 2020, two days ago. 'I visited Rome last summer.'
existing_questions_sample: I ____ (see) that film last week. | saw
I ____ (see) that film three times. I love it! | have seen
We have lived here ____ 2018. (for / since) | since
She has had that phone ____ two years. (for / since) | for
How long ____ you known Marta? (have / did / do) | have
Correct it: I have called him yesterday. | I called him yesterday.
They ____ (move) to Madrid in 2015. | moved
He's been ill ____ Tuesday. (for / since) | since
'Have you ever been to London?' 'Yes, I ____ (go) there last year.' | went
Correct it: We are friends since May. | We have been friends since May.
My grandparents have been married ____ a long time. (for / since) | for
When ____ you buy those trainers? (have / did) | did

units.grammar: will and be going to. will / won't + infinitive is for general predictions and opinions about the future, often after I think, I'm sure or probably: 'I think robots will do most jobs.' will is also for decisions made at the moment of speaking, offers and promises: 'It's hot in here - I'll open the window.' be going to is for plans you decided before speaking: 'I'm going to visit my aunt on Saturday. I've already told her.'
existing_questions_sample: 'The phone is ringing.' 'OK, I ____ (answer) it.' Use will or going to. | will answer
We've bought the paint. We ____ (paint) the kitchen this weekend. Use will or going to. | are going to paint
I think Spain ____ (win) the next World Cup. Use will. | will win
Look at those black clouds! It ____ (rain). Use will or going to. | is going to rain
Correct it: She wills come later. | She will come later.
Don't worry, I ____ (not / tell) anyone your secret. Use will. | won't tell
____ people live on Mars one day? (Will / Are / Do) | Will
Correct it: I will to help you. | I will help you.
'I'm thirsty.' 'Wait, I ____ (get) you some water.' Use will or going to. | will get
I've decided: I ____ (study) biology at university. Use will or going to. | am going to study
In 2080 there ____ (not / be) any petrol cars, I think. Use will. | won't be
Be careful! The ladder is moving. You ____ (fall)! Use will or going to. | are going to fall

units.grammar: Modals of probability. Modal verbs of probability show how sure you are. They never change form and are followed by an infinitive without to: 'She must be at home.' must = I'm almost certain it is true: 'You've run ten kilometres. You must be thirsty.' might / could = it is possible, but I'm not sure: 'Take an umbrella. It might rain.' 'This could be the right street.'
existing_questions_sample: He's wearing a coat and gloves. He ____ be cold. (must / can't) | must
That ____ be the postman. He never comes on Sundays. (must / can't) | can't
I'm not sure where Ana is. She ____ be in the library. (might / must) | might
Correct it: She must to be tired. | She must be tired.
You've just eaten a huge pizza! You ____ be hungry again. (can't / must) | can't
Correct it: It mights rain tomorrow. | It might rain tomorrow.
Their lights are on, so they ____ be at home. (must / can't) | must
Perhaps this key opens the door. = This key ____ open the door. (could / can't) | could
Correct it: That mustn't be true. It's impossible! | That can't be true.
It's possible that he doesn't know. = He ____ know. (might not / can't) | might not
I'm certain this is Dad's jacket. = This ____ be Dad's jacket. (must / might) | must
I'm sure that isn't Mia's bag; hers is red. = It ____ be Mia's bag. (can't / might) | can't

units.grammar: just, already and yet. just, already and yet are used with the present perfect (have / has + past participle). just = a very short time ago. It goes between have / has and the participle: 'The bus has just left.' already = before now, or sooner than expected. It normally goes between have / has and the participle, sometimes at the end: 'I've already seen this episode.'
existing_questions_sample: I haven't finished my project ____. (yet / already / just) | yet
'Do you want a sandwich?' 'No, thanks. I've ____ eaten.' (already / yet) | already
The floor is wet because I've ____ cleaned it. (just / yet) | just
Have you done the washing-up ____? (yet / just / already) | yet
Put 'just' in the right place: She has arrived. | She has just arrived.
Put 'yet' in the right place: They haven't called. | They haven't called yet.
Put 'already' before the main verb: We have bought the tickets. | We have already bought the tickets.
Correct it: I haven't already eaten. | I haven't eaten yet.
Correct it: He has just go out. | He has just gone out.
It's only ten o'clock and she has ____ done all her work! (already / yet) | already
'Is Tom here?' 'No, he's ____ left. You missed him by a minute.' (just / yet) | just
Hurry up! The match ____ (just / start). | has just started

units.grammar: Relative clauses. A relative clause tells us which person, thing or place we mean: 'The girl who sits next to me is from Peru.' Use who or that for people: 'a doctor who / that works with children'. Use which or that for things: 'the bus which / that goes to the centre'. Use where for places: 'This is the café where we had breakfast.'
existing_questions_sample: She's the teacher ____ helped me. (who / which / where) | who
This is the phone ____ I bought yesterday. (who / which / where) | which
That's the park ____ we play football. (who / which / where) | where
Correct it: That's the book that I read it. | That's the book that I read.
A baker is a person ____ makes bread. (who / which) | who
A fridge is a machine ____ keeps food cold. (who / which) | which
Join with 'where': That's the hotel. We stayed there. = That's the hotel ____. | where we stayed
Which word can replace 'who'? The boy who called you is my cousin. (that / which / where) | that
Is this the shop ____ you lost your wallet? (which / where / who) | where
Correct it: She's the girl who she won. | She's the girl who won.
I like films ____ make me laugh. (who / that / where) | that
Join with 'who': I have a friend. He speaks Chinese. = I have a friend ____. | who speaks Chinese

units.grammar: Present simple passive. Form: am / is / are + past participle. 'Rice is grown in Asia.' 'These cars are made in Germany.' Negative: isn't / aren't + participle. Question: Is / Are + subject + participle? 'Is French spoken in Canada?' Use the passive when the action or the object is more important than who does it, or when we don't know who does it: 'The rubbish is collected on Mondays.'
existing_questions_sample: Cheese ____ (make) from milk. | is made
Millions of emails ____ (send) every minute. | are sent
English ____ (speak) in Australia. | is spoken
The classrooms ____ (not / clean) at weekends. | aren't cleaned
____ these phones made in China? (Is / Are / Do) | Are
Correct it: The rooms is cleaned daily. | The rooms are cleaned daily.
Correct it: Paper is make from wood. | Paper is made from wood.
Make it passive: People grow coffee in Brazil. = Coffee ____ in Brazil. | is grown
Make it passive: They sell tickets online. = Tickets ____ online. | are sold
Active or passive? 'The museum is visited by many tourists.' | passive
This programme ____ (watch) by millions of people. | is watched
Where ____ bananas grown? (is / are / do) | are

units.grammar: Zero and first conditional. Conditional sentences have an if-clause (the condition) and a result clause. Either can come first; use a comma when the if-clause is first. Zero conditional: if + present simple, present simple. It is for things that are always true: 'If you mix blue and yellow, you get green.'
existing_questions_sample: If you heat ice, it ____ (melt). | melts
If it rains tomorrow, we ____ (stay) at home. | will stay
If she ____ (study) hard, she'll pass the exam. | studies
Correct it: If it will rain, we'll stay. | If it rains, we'll stay.
You won't pass ____ you study. (if / unless) | unless
Plants die if they ____ (not / get) water. | don't get
I ____ (not / go) to the beach if it's cold tomorrow. | won't go
If you ____ (not / hurry), you'll miss the train. | don't hurry
What ____ you do if the shop is closed? (will / do / are) | will
Dad is definitely coming. ____ he arrives, we'll have dinner. (If / When) | When
If you press this button, the light ____ (come) on. It always works. | comes
Unless it ____ (stop) raining, we won't play. | stops

units.grammar: Reported commands. To report an order, a request or advice, use: reporting verb + person + to + infinitive. 'Sit down!' - 'The teacher told us to sit down.' For negatives use not to + infinitive: 'Don't shout!' - 'She told them not to shout.' Common reporting verbs: tell (orders), ask (polite requests), advise (advice), and also warn, remind, persuade, encourage and convince.
existing_questions_sample: 'Close the window.' - He told me ____ the window. | to close
'Don't be late.' - Mum told us ____ late. | not to be
'Please help me.' - She ____ me to help her. (said / asked) | asked
Correct it: He said me to wait. | He told me to wait.
Correct it: She told me to not run. | She told me not to run.
'You should rest.' - The doctor advised him ____. | to rest
'Don't touch the dog!' - He warned us ____ the dog. | not to touch
Correct it: Dad told to me to stop. | Dad told me to stop.
'Please don't tell anyone.' - She asked me ____ anyone. | not to tell
'Bring your books.' - The teacher reminded us ____ our books. | to bring
'Tidy your room!' - Mum told me to tidy ____ room. (your / my / her) | my
Correct it: They asked us waiting outside. | They asked us to wait outside.

units.grammar: Second conditional. Form: if + past simple, would / wouldn't + infinitive. 'If I had a boat, I would sail around the world.' Use it for imaginary, unreal or unlikely situations in the present or future. It does not talk about the past. Either clause can come first; use a comma when the if-clause is first. The short form of would is 'd: 'I'd buy it if it was cheaper.'
existing_questions_sample: If I ____ (have) more time, I would learn Japanese. | had
If she won the lottery, she ____ (buy) a castle. | would buy
What ____ you do if you lost your phone? (will / would / did) | would
If I ____ you, I'd talk to the teacher. (am / were / would be) | were
Correct it: If I would know, I'd tell you. | If I knew, I'd tell you.
We ____ (not / be) late every day if we lived nearer. | wouldn't be
If he ____ (not / play) so many video games, he'd sleep better. | didn't play
Correct it: If I could, I will help. | If I could, I would help.
I ____ (travel) more if flights were cheaper. | would travel
If animals ____ (can) talk, what would they say? | could
Would you be scared if you ____ (see) a shark? | saw
Real or imaginary? 'If I were invisible, I'd travel for free.' | imaginary

units.grammar: Reported speech. When you report what someone said, the verb usually moves one step back into the past: present simple - past simple; present continuous - past continuous; will - would; can - could. 'I like jazz,' said Ben. - 'Ben said (that) he liked jazz.' The word that is optional. Pronouns and possessives change to fit the situation: 'I'll call my mum,' said Eva. - 'Eva said she would call her mum.'
existing_questions_sample: 'I live in Leeds,' said Tom. - Tom said he ____ in Leeds. | lived
'We are watching TV,' they said. - They said they ____ TV. | were watching
'I will help you,' said Ana. - Ana said she ____ help me. | would
'I can swim,' said the boy. - The boy said he ____ swim. | could
She ____ me that she was hungry. (said / told) | told
He ____ that he didn't like fish. (said / told) | said
Correct it: She said me she was busy. | She told me she was busy.
'I love my new bike,' said Leo. - Leo said he loved ____ new bike. (my / his / your) | his
'We don't have any money,' they said. - They said they ____ any money. | didn't have
'It is raining,' said Mum. - Mum said it ____. | was raining
'I won't be late,' said Dan. - Dan said he ____ be late. | wouldn't
Correct it: He said he will come. | He said he would come.

units.grammar: Past simple passive. Form: was / were + past participle. 'The bridge was built in 1900.' 'The windows were broken.' Negative: wasn't / weren't + participle. Question: Was / Were + subject + participle? 'Was the thief caught?' Use it when the action is more important than the person who did it, or when we don't know who did it: 'My bike was stolen last night.'
existing_questions_sample: The first iPhone ____ (sell) in 2007. | was sold
These pyramids ____ (build) thousands of years ago. | were built
The window ____ (not / break) by the children. | wasn't broken
____ the emails sent yesterday? (Was / Were / Did) | Were
'Don Quixote' was written ____ Cervantes. (by / from / for) | by
Correct it: The cake was ate. | The cake was eaten.
Correct it: Two men was arrested. | Two men were arrested.
Make it passive: Someone stole my wallet. = My wallet ____. | was stolen
Make it passive: They found the paintings in a garage. = The paintings ____ in a garage. | were found
When ____ this school opened? (was / were / did) | was
Make it active: The goal was scored by Alba. = Alba ____ the goal. | scored
We ____ (not / invite) to the wedding. | weren't invited
